terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js fills a workshop and books two groups on a fresh copy of the studio's data.

tasks.title: Refuse a booking when the workshop is full
tasks.description:
Change `book(workshopId, name)` in `src/store.js`: when the workshop has no places left, it adds nothing and returns `{ problem: 'full' }`. Everything else stays as it is: a workshop with places left takes the booking, and one that is not there is `{ problem: 'not_found' }`.

The route answers 409 for `full`. The check books the last place of a workshop, then one more, tries a workshop that is full to the last seat and one with every place free, and looks at the bookings table.
nextSteps: Look at its places left before anything is added.
Return the problem when none are left.
Run `node try.js` and look at the seventh booking.
hints: `get` already gives each workshop its `placesLeft`, counted for that workshop only.
The check has to come before the `INSERT`: once the row is in, the booking has happened. No place left means `placesLeft` is less than 1.
`const workshop = get(workshopId)`, `if (!workshop) return { problem: 'not_found' }`, then `if (workshop.placesLeft < 1) return { problem: 'full' }` before the insert.

tasks.title: Book a group, all or none
tasks.description:
Implement `bookGroup(workshopId, names)` in `src/store.js`. `names` is a list of one or more names, already checked by the route.

- when the workshop has at least as many places left as there are names, it books every name and returns `{ bookings: [...] }`, each `{ id, workshopId, name }` in the order of the names
- when it has fewer, it books nobody and returns `{ problem: 'full' }`
- when there is no such workshop, it returns `{ problem: 'not_found' }`

Each value reaches the database in the place of a `?`. The check sends groups that fit, one too big, one that takes the last places exactly and one for a workshop that is not there, each on a fresh database, and looks at the bookings table.
nextSteps: Read the workshop and return the problem when it is not there.
Compare its places left with the size of the whole group.
Book every name with one prepared `INSERT`.
Return the bookings and run `node try.js`.
hints: Booking the names one by one with `book` stops when the workshop fills up, after some of the group are already in.
Decide about the group once, before the first booking: `names.length` against `placesLeft`. Then a prepared statement can run once per name.
`if (workshop.placesLeft < names.length) return { problem: 'full' }`, then `names.map((name) => ({ id: insert.run(workshopId, name).lastInsertRowid, workshopId, name }))`.

tasks.title: Undo a group that fails halfway
tasks.description:
Make `bookGroup` all or nothing even when the database fails in the middle of a group:

- when any booking of the group fails, no booking of that group stays in the table
- the error goes on, so the error handler logs it and answers 500
- afterwards the next booking works and is saved as usual
- a group that is refused, as too big or for a workshop that is not there, leaves no transaction open either

The check makes the database fail on the second booking of a group, then books one more place. It also refuses a group and books one more place after it.
nextSteps: Start a transaction before the first booking of the group.
Keep the changes once every booking has gone in.
Undo them when one of the bookings throws.
Let the error go on, and run `node try.js`.
hints: Until a transaction is kept, its changes can still be thrown away together. Every way out of `bookGroup` has to end the transaction, one way or the other.
`db.exec('BEGIN')`, `db.exec('COMMIT')` and `db.exec('ROLLBACK')` start, keep and undo a transaction. A `try` around the bookings with a `catch` lets you undo them when one throws.
`db.exec('BEGIN')`, then `try { ...the bookings...; db.exec('COMMIT'); return { bookings } } catch (err) { db.exec('ROLLBACK'); throw err }`.
